newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH UNIPETROL SEES GROSS 1997 PROFIT AT 3.7 BLN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH UNIPETROL SEES GROSS 1997 PROFIT AT 3.7 BLN.

text.p: Czech petrochemical group Unipetrol a.s., expected to be listed soon on the Prague Stock Exchange, has forecast gross consolidated pre-tax profit for 1997 of 3.7 billion crowns, financial director Radomil Stepanek told a news conference on Friday.
"(We expect) consolidated profit before tax, including new minority holdings, of 3.7 billion (crowns)," Stepanek said.
Unipetrol has applied for a listing on the Prague Stock Exchange's main market, following the merger of Kaucuk Group a.s. and Chempetrol Group a.s. .
The listing, which would be one of the highest capitalised issues on the market, will be considered at a meeting of the PSE listing committee on August 8.
Trading in shares of Kaucuk and Chemopetrol ended after last Friday's session on the PSE, as the merger, approved earlier this year, was finalised under Czech law.
Stepanek said the company expected nominal 100-crown shares in Unipetrol to open in September on the PSE at between 110-120 crowns, but the actual opening price is up to PSE officials.

Unipetrol chief executive Miroslav Tera told the news conference that a further part of the 65 percent in Unipetrol still held by the government as part of the complicated Czech petrochemical privatisation programme, might be sold by the end of this year.
He did not give further details and any privatisation decision is up to the Czech government.
